claims.text: The long-term stability of a protective oxide on single-phase CrFeCoNiX above 900 °C is governed by selective oxidation of X in concert with Cr.
Al is more effective than Si or Mn at enabling the proposed selective-oxidation mechanism.
Preferential oxidation produces a scale whose phase composition has favorable thermal-expansion and lattice matching with the CrFeCoNiX substrate.
Favorable thermal-expansion and lattice matching reduce interfacial stress and thereby suppress oxide cracking and spallation.
The proposed alloys have a single-phase metallic solid-solution initial state.
X is a minor alloy addition in CrFeCoNiX.
Changing X among Si, Mn, and Al will alter oxide growth kinetics and interfacial stresses above 900 °C.
An Al-containing alloy can form a continuous alumina-rich protective surface layer.
A Si-containing alloy can form a related protective silicate scale.
Preferential oxidation of X together with Cr produces an oxide with reduced thermal-expansion mismatch and improved chemical inertness.
High configurational entropy of the alloy promotes a uniform cation distribution in the resulting oxide scale.
High configurational entropy of the alloy dictates tailored oxidation pathways during scale formation.
The proposed composition and structure of the scale cause it to grow slowly while remaining coherent.
A CrFeCoNiX alloy with an appropriate minor addition, especially Al, will form a thin, adherent, slow-growing scale resistant to cracking and spallation.
Mn- or Si-containing variants that do not form comparably coherent oxides will exhibit more frequent scale breakdown than the favorable Al-containing variant.
CrFeCoNi without X is the proposed baseline for isolating the effect of the added element.
Failure of the beneficial-X alloy to outperform the CrFeCoNi baseline and the other X variants in scale stability, coherence, and growth rate would count against the proposed mechanism.
